_comment: Authorization policy for the two-button demo WITH the proof gate (18012-3
11.2.4). Read-only in the gateway: these tables are memoryType 'sp' (Secret
Programmed) -- secret, preset, and not changeable over HES-CLME.
Identical to auth_policy_two_buttons.json -- same classes, credential, groups
and permissions -- plus one addition: the 'proofRequired' section.
18012-3 has nowhere to say 'this operation must be accompanied by a proof of
the sender's identity'. Table 68 (permissionService) says what a class may do,
never how it must prove itself, and Table 64 (credentials) has no field for a
public key. So the requirement is declared here, in this document's own
section, rather than by inventing a transCode or an extra key inside a
Each entry names a binding-map authorType address ('at') and the public ID
('pi', 64 hex characters) that the proof must demonstrate. Presence makes a
proof MANDATORY for that target -- forgetting to send one is a denial, not a
silent pass. Absence means nothing changes.
The requirement is a SECOND gate, on top of the permission check: a message
must still carry a credential the permission tables accept. The proof is not
an alternative way to be authorized.
